title: Return of the Loss-of-Use Charge on a Cancelled HomeFlood Policy
content:
**Rule.** When a HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies policy is cancelled on the named insured's signed request, the loss-of-use return is the part of the premium return that comes from the tier's annual loss-of-use charge, which forms part of the term premium item. The loss-of-use share is that charge taken in the same proportion of the premium return as the term premium booked for the term.

| Claim payments on the policy for losses dated fewer than 12 whole months before the processing date | Loss-of-use return |
|---|---|
| a claim paid loss-of-use money, net of voided payments | nothing |
| claims paid other coverages, but no loss-of-use money | 50 percent of the loss-of-use share |
| otherwise | the full share |

**The processing date.** The processing date is the day the cancellation is processed and recorded, and every window counted to the processing date ends on that day. A loss falls in the window when the whole calendar months from its date of loss to the processing date are fewer than 12. A count of whole calendar months runs from the earlier date to the later one; the last month is not counted when the later date's day of the month falls before the earlier date's day of the month.

**Net payments.** Loss-of-use money is payment on the loss-of-use coverage, net of voided payments. A loss-of-use payment that was voided in full leaves no loss-of-use money.

*Hypothetical illustration:* on a HomeFlood Standard policy with a loss-of-use charge of 45 per year, where the premium return is 40 percent of the term premium booked, the loss-of-use share is 18.00. When a dwelling claim was paid in the window with no loss-of-use money, the loss-of-use return is 50 percent of that share, 9.00.
